message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results using Apple's own newsroom release and its FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR. The primary sources show Q4 FY2024 revenue of **$94.9B, up 6% year over year** — an acceleration from full-year growth — and FY2024 total net sales of **$391.0B** (vs. $383.3B), net income of **$93.7B**, diluted EPS of **$6.08**, and operating income of **$123.2B**. EPS was held down by a one-time **$10.2B** tax charge in the quarter, meaning underlying profitability was better than the headline EPS comparison suggests; the core franchise remains highly cash-generative with a huge installed base and the Apple Intelligence rollout as a potential iPhone 16 upgrade catalyst. I explicitly discarded a search hit from "earnings-preview-hub.com" claiming management guided FY2025 to $9.50 EPS and 25%+ revenue growth — it was a single, uncorroborated source that conflicts with Apple's own disclosures and is arithmetically implausible, so I did not rely on it. News flow otherwise described shares as steady near $222 on iPhone 16 demand and a phased Apple Intelligence rollout, and the live quote confirmed $222.70 last with a $222.72 ask, so I bought **44 shares of AAPL at a $223.00 limit** (≈$9,812, inside the $10,000 per-order cap, with no other orders today so total spend is well under $20,000). The limit sat about 0.1% above the market and the order filled at $223.00; cash remains ample at roughly $40,188 and I did not move any money out of the account.
